mainTopic: Can a vow be undone before it has taken effect? The difference between a husband's הפרה and a חכם's שאלה (התרה).
overview: The amud closes a story in which רב אחא בר רב הוּנא let a man's vow take effect, covering him with clay, before bringing him to רב חסדא to have it undone. רבא praises this move. He explains that רב אחא held that the argument between רבי נתן and the רבנן about a husband's הפרה before a vow takes effect also applies to שאלה before a חכם. רב פפי disagrees and says the argument is only about הפרה. For שאלה, everyone agrees the vow must already have taken effect, based on 'לא יחל דברו'. The גמרא tries to support רב פפי from two ברייתות that require two linked vows to be asked about in a set order. The first proof is pushed aside because the ברייתא never says which vow counts as 'first.' The second is pushed aside because that ברייתא may follow רבי נתן alone. Finally, רבינא reports, through מרימר, a second version of רב פפי with the opposite rule: everyone agrees a חכם can release a vow even before it takes effect, also based on 'לא יחל דברו'. The explanation of how that פסוק teaches this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the story: smeared with clay and brought to רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב הוּנא smears the man with clay and brings him before רב חסדא to have his vow undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he smeared him with clay, and brought him before רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes a story that began earlier. רב אחא בר רב הוּנא covers the man in clay and then brings him to רב חסדא so the vow can be undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's vow forbade him from benefiting from the world, so wearing clothes was now forbidden to him. Covering him with clay kept him protected without breaking the vow. The key point is that the vow had already taken effect before he was brought to the חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: before him (in front of a rabbi)

phrases.english: And he smeared him with clay,
phrases.notes: His vow now forbade benefit from the world, so clothes were off-limits; the clay protected him instead.

phrases.english: and brought him before Rav Chisda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vow was allowed to take effect, and only then was the man brought to a חכם to have it undone.

steps.title: רבא explains why רב אחא's plan was wise
steps.stepSummary: רבא praises רב אחא בר רב הוּנא. He explains that רב אחא held the argument between רבי נתן and the רבנן about הפרה also applies to שאלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Who would be wise enough to do something like this, if not רב אחא בר רב הוּנא, who is a great man? He holds that just as the רבנן and רבי נתן argue about הפרה, they also argue about שאלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא praises the story's move and explains the thinking behind it. רב אחא made the vow take effect first because, according to רבי נתן, a vow cannot be undone before it takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן and the רבנן argue about whether a husband can do הפרה on a vow that has not yet taken effect. רב אחא assumed the same argument applies when a חכם undoes a vow through שאלה. So he made sure the vow took effect first, which satisfies everyone's view.

keyTerms.meaning: a husband (or father) cancelling a vow
asking a חכם to undo a vow

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the central question of this section: does the rule for הפרה carry over to שאלה?

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן חַכִּים לְמִיעְבַּד כִּי הָא מִילְּתָא
phrases.english: Who is wise enough to do a thing like this

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: if not Rav Acha bar Rav Huna,
who is a great man?
For he holds that just as
the Rabbis and Rabbi Natan argue about nullification,
phrases.notes: Their argument is whether a husband can cancel a vow that hasn't taken effect yet.

phrases.english: so too they argue about asking a sage to release a vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן חַכִּים לְמִיעְבַּד כִּי הָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the action in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב אחא (as רבא explains him), the argument between רבי נתן and the רבנן about undoing a vow before it takes effect applies to both הפרה and שאלה.

steps.title: רב פפי: the argument is only about הפרה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי limits the argument to הפרה. רבי נתן requires the vow to have taken effect, and the רבנן allow הפרה even before. Each side has a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: The argument is about הפרה. רבי נתן holds that a husband can only do הפרה once the vow has taken effect, as it says 'וחפרה הלבנה'. The רבנן hold that a husband can do הפרה even before the vow takes effect, as it says 'מפר מחשבות ערומים'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי gives a different view from רבא's explanation. He says the argument between רבי נתן and the רבנן is only about a husband's הפרה, and he gives each side's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן reads 'חפרה' (the moon is confounded) as a hint to הפרה. The moon already exists, so only a vow that already exists can be cancelled. The רבנן point to 'מפר מחשבות', which shows הפרה can work even on mere plans, meaning a vow that has not yet taken effect.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappi said:
The argument is about nullification only,
for Rabbi Natan holds:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַבַּעַל מֵיפֵר אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן חָל נֶדֶר,
phrases.english: a husband cannot nullify unless the vow has taken effect,
as it is written: “And the moon shall be confounded.”
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 24:23. The word חפרה sounds like הפרה, and notice that the moon already exists.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל מֵיפֵר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא חָל נֶדֶר,
phrases.english: a husband can nullify even though the vow has not taken effect,
as it is written: “He nullifies the plans of the crafty.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבא's view that the argument also applies to שאלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between רבי נתן and the רבנן is limited to הפרה. רבי נתן requires the vow to have taken effect, and the רבנן do not.

steps.title: For שאלה, everyone agrees the vow must take effect first
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי continues: for a חכם's release of a vow, everyone agrees the vow must already have taken effect, based on 'לא יחל דברו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for שאלה, everyone agrees that a חכם cannot release anything unless the vow has taken effect, as it says 'לא יחל דברו'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי finishes his point. With a חכם, there is no argument at all, and the vow must already exist before it can be released.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'his word,' meaning a vow that is already in place. The power of a חכם to release a vow works only on such an existing vow. So according to רב פפי, the רבנן's leniency for הפרה does not carry over to שאלה.

keyTerms.meaning: he shall not break his word

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's view (explaining רב אחא): the argument about undoing a vow before it takes effect applies to both הפרה and שאלה. רב פפי: the argument is only about הפרה, and for שאלה everyone requires the vow to have taken effect.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up הפרה and שאלה. הפרה is done by a husband or father, while שאלה (התרה) is done by a חכם. The whole argument here is whether the same rule applies to both.

phrases.english: But regarding asking a sage —
everyone agrees
a sage cannot release anything
unless the vow has taken effect,
as it is written: “He shall not break his word.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפי's statement by giving the rule for שאלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that a חכם can only release a vow that has already taken effect.

steps.title: A ברייתא about two linked vows seems to support רב פפי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a ברייתא supports רב פפי. Someone who vowed off benefit from a person, and also from whichever חכם he asks to release that vow, must ask about the first vow first and only then about the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a ברייתא supports him? 'קונם, I will not benefit from so-and-so, nor from whoever I ask to release it.' He asks about the first, and afterwards about the second. If you say one can ask even before the vow takes effect, he could ask about either one first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a proof for רב פפי from a ברייתא that requires a fixed order. This is presented as a suggestion ("shall we say"), so it may still be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second vow (against the חכם he asks) only takes effect once he actually asks a חכם about the first vow. If a חכם could release a vow before it takes effect, the order would not matter. The ברייתא insists on the order, which fits רב פפי's view that שאלה requires the vow to have taken effect.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say this supports him?
a vow formula making something forbidden like a קָרְבָּן
he asks (a חָכָם to release a vow)

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
“Konam, that I will not benefit from so-and-so,
and from whoever I ask about it” —
phrases.notes: He means the חכם he will later ask to release the first vow.

phrases.english: he asks about the first,
and afterwards he asks about the second.
And if you say one may ask

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא חָל נֶדֶר,
phrases.english: even though the vow has not taken effect,

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי — עַל הַאי נִיתְּשִׁיל בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: if he wants, let him ask about this one first,

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי — עַל הַאי נִיתְּשִׁיל בְּרֵישָׁא.
phrases.english: and if he wants, let him ask about that one first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רב פפי's view about שאלה.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפי's claim that a חכם can only release a vow that has already taken effect.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about two vows, where the second (against the חכם asked) only takes effect after he asks about the first. It requires asking about the first vow before the second.

steps.title: The first ברייתא does not prove which vow counts as first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the ברייתא in step 5. The words 'first' and 'second' may not mean the order in which the vows were made.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do we know which vow is the 'first' one and which is the 'last' one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 5. It says the ברייתא never told us which vow is really 'first'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 assumed the ברייתא means he must undo the earlier vow before the later one. That would show a vow must take effect before it can be released. But the ברייתא may only mean he asks about one vow and then the other, in any order he chooses. If so, there is no proof for רב פפי.

keyTerms.meaning: And who knows? It shows we cannot be sure.

phrases.english: And who knows if this one is the first
phrases.notes: He means: the ברייתא never says which vow it calls 'first.' It may just mean whichever one he asks about first.

phrases.english: or if that one is the last?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רב פפי's view itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's 'first' and 'second' may describe the order he chooses for asking, not the order the vows were made.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: the vow of נזירות that depends on asking to undo the first vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a man who vowed off benefit from someone. He also said he would become a נזיר once he asks to undo that vow. The ברייתא says he must ask about the first vow, then about the נזירות. This seems to show a vow cannot be released before it takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let us say a different ברייתא supports רב פפי. A man said: 'It is קונם that I may not benefit from so-and-so, and I am a נזיר once I ask a חכם to undo this vow.' He asks about his vow first, and only afterward about his נזירות. If you say a person can ask for release even before the vow has taken effect, he should be able to start with either one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof for רב פפי. It uses a ברייתא where the vow of נזירות has not started yet when he first asks about the other vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזירות only begins once he asks a חכם to undo the קונם vow. So before that, the נזירות has not taken effect. The ברייתא requires him to ask about the קונם first. That suggests a חכם cannot release the נזירות while it has not yet taken effect, which fits רב פפי's claim in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used to make a vow that forbids something
A person who has vowed נזירות (no wine, no haircut, no contact with the dead)
When I ask (a חכם to undo my vow)

phrases.english: Rather, let us say this supports him:
"It is konam that I will not benefit from so-and-so,
and I am a nazirite once I ask for release from it" —
he asks about his vow,
and afterward he asks about his naziriteship.
And if you say he can ask for release

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא חָל נֶדֶר,
phrases.english: even though the vow has not taken effect,

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי — עַל נִדְרוֹ אִיתְּשִׁיל בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: if he wants, he can ask about his vow first,

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי — עַל נִזְרוֹ אִיתְּשִׁיל בְּרֵישָׁא!
phrases.english: and if he wants, he can ask about his naziriteship first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed in step 6, the גמרא offers a new proof for the same view.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפי's claim that a חכם can only release a vow after it has taken effect
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a vow of נזירות that depends on asking to undo a קונם vow, where the required order is the קונם first

steps.title: The ברייתא may follow רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא may follow רבי נתן, who holds a vow must take effect before it can be undone. So it does not prove that everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns aside the proof from step 7 with a short answer: this ברייתא is רבי נתן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפי claimed that for a חכם's release, everyone agrees the vow must already have taken effect. But a ברייתא that fits only רבי נתן cannot prove that the רבנן agree too. So the ברייתא does not support רב פפי's claim that everyone agrees.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Natan.
phrases.notes: רבי נתן holds a vow must take effect before it can be undone, so this ברייתא fits him alone.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The ברייתא can still be true according to רבי נתן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may follow only one side of the argument, so it cannot show that everyone agrees.

steps.title: A second version of רב פפי: a חכם can release even before the vow takes effect
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports, through מרימר, a different version of רב פפי's teaching. The argument between רבי נתן and the רבנן is only about הפרה. For שאלה, everyone agrees a חכם can release a vow even before it takes effect, based on 'לא יחל דברו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: מרימר told me that your father said this in the name of רב פפי. The argument is about הפרה. But about asking a חכם, everyone agrees he can undo the vow even though it has not taken effect, as it says 'לא יחל דברו'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a second version of רב פפי's teaching. Its conclusion is the opposite of the version in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that רבי נתן and the רבנן argue only about הפרה. In step 4, everyone agreed a חכם needs the vow to have taken effect. Here, everyone agrees a חכם does not need that. The same פסוק, 'לא יחל דברו', is used as the source, and the גמרא will now explain how.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband or father cancelling a vow
Asking a חכם to release a vow

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions of רב פפי. In step 4, everyone agrees a חכם can only release a vow after it takes effect. In this version, everyone agrees a חכם can release it even before it takes effect.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the question of releasing a vow before it takes effect has two opposite traditions in רב פפי's name. Both are built on the same פסוק.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Mareimar said to me,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אֲמַר אֲבוּךְ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פַּפִּי:
phrases.english: this is what your father said in the name of Rav Pappi:
phrases.notes: "Your father" is רבינא's father. מרימר is telling רבינא what his own father taught.

phrases.english: The argument is about nullification,
but about asking a sage, everyone agrees he can undo it

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא חָל נֶדֶר,
phrases.english: even though the vow has not taken effect,
as it is written: "He shall not profane his word."
phrases.notes: במדבר 30:3. The גמרא is about to explain how this פסוק shows it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אָמַר לִי מָרִימָר, הָכִי אֲמַר אֲבוּךְ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פַּפִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs for the first version of רב פפי failed, the גמרא brings a competing version of what רב פפי said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נתן and the רבנן argue only about הפרה. For a חכם's release, everyone agrees he can release a vow even before it has taken effect, based on 'לא יחל דברו'.
